svg.aria-label: How a warp is divided among element solves
svg.title: How a warp is divided among element solves
svg.text: A warp = 8 groups of 4 lanes; each group solves one 8×8 element system
The two kernel families fill a warp's 8 groups differently. Lanes are colored by their index within the group.
coop_256: one block per (angle a, group g); the 8 groups take 8 different elements of the hyperplane
dag kernels: one warp per (angle a, element e); the 8 groups are 8 energy groups of that element
dag: the 8 groups read the same A, B, M0 rows, F blocks and face table entries, so those loads are shared by the whole warp.
Inside one group: lane l owns rows l and l + 4 of the system
• 2 rows × 8 entries + 2 entries of b per lane, held in registers
• row kk lives in lane kk % 4, slot kk / 4: compile-time constants in the
unrolled loops, so no indexing cost
• the LU step broadcasts each pivot row with __shfl_sync inside the group
• 4 lanes (rather than 8 or 1) balances registers per lane against how
many elements a warp solves at once
